question: Progression from MCI to AD among ADNI MCI participants (Alzheimer's-spectrum MCI in both; ADNI1/GO/2/3 in both, so participants overlap). The shared channel is MRI: P-356 uses three axial T1 slices through the hippocampus alone; P-244's model concatenates baseline clinical features (cognitive scores, APOE4 and others) with FreeSurfer regional surface area, volume and thickness. Under the rule a multimodal model matches when the compared channel is shared (as applied in C-103). Differences in features, architecture, label construction (cleaned stable/progressive dichotomy vs censored survival data), validation design and horizon are allowed and are listed below.
metric: ROC-AUC with ROC-AUC. P-356's is a binary AUC for conversion within 36 months against stability for at least 3 years; P-244's is a time-dependent AUC from a survival model at fixed horizons (3 and 5 years), with censored participants included. Same metric type; the estimand difference is recorded as a candidate explanation.

figures.P-356: ViT on three hippocampal T1 slices: test AUC 0.74 +/- 0.02 over 10 runs (range 0.72-0.78); accuracy 0.69. No interval printed. Test set = 15% of 575 subjects, about 86 (41 pMCI, 45 sMCI at the constant class ratio). Hanley-McNeil, A = 0.74: Q1 = 0.74/1.26 = 0.5873, Q2 = 2(0.5476)/1.74 = 0.6294; SE^2 = [0.74*0.26 + 40(0.5873-0.5476) + 44(0.6294-0.5476)]/(41*45) = 5.381/1845, SE = 0.0540; 95% CI [0.634, 0.846]. The best of the 10 runs (0.78) also lies below every P-244 bound below. 3D ResNet-18 on the same task: 0.75 (CI about [0.646, 0.854]).
figures.P-244: Deep-AD, 783 ADNI MCI (348 converters, 435 censored), five-fold CV. Time-dependent AUC for MCI->AD: 3 years 0.914, 5 years 0.957 (the record's figure). No AUC interval printed; the class sizes at each horizon are not printed. Hanley-McNeil for 0.914, bracketed: narrowest with all 348 events against 435 censored, Q1 = 0.914/1.086 = 0.8416, Q2 = 2(0.8354)/1.914 = 0.8729, SE^2 = [0.914*0.086 + 347(0.8416-0.8354) + 434(0.8729-0.8354)]/(348*435) = 18.53/151380, SE = 0.0111, CI [0.892, 0.936]; widest plausible at one fold's size (70/87), SE = 0.0248, CI [0.865, 0.963]; even at 50 three-year cases against 87 controls, CI [0.858, 0.971]. 5-year 0.957 at fold size: CI [0.923, 0.992]. For reference, the C-index is 0.718 (95% CI 0.712-0.725) for the discovered patterns as a single CPH variable, and the AIBL external C-index 0.752 (0.698-0.807).

matched_figure_check: A horizon-matched figure exists and does not reconcile the pair. The record sets P-356's 36-month AUC against P-244's 5-year AUC (0.957), but P-244 also prints a 3-year AUC (0.914), which matches P-356's 36-month window; 0.914 still lies far outside P-356's interval [0.634, 0.846], and 0.74 lies outside P-244's 3-year interval at any plausible n (lowest bound 0.858). No input-matched figure exists: P-244 reports no MRI-only model in the held text (its only reduced models are single-variable survival models on MMSE, 0.537-0.600, and APOE4, 0.564-0.681, which are neither the MRI channel nor near P-356), and P-356 reports no clinical-feature model. P-244's comparisons with other machine-learning models are in Supplementary Tables S6-S8, which are not part of the held source. Neither paper therefore reproduces the other's condition, and neither shows that any one difference accounts for the gap.
performance_validity: Neither study meets the Section 3.5 exclusion, checked on the sources. P-244's compared AUCs are 0.914 (3 years) and 0.957 (5 years), below 0.97; its 10-year AUC range reaches 0.979 but is not the compared figure; its sample is 783 MCI participants and it has an external AIBL check (reported as a C-index). P-356's AUC is 0.74 from a subject-level split of 575 participants.

candidate_explanations.difference: Predictor set: P-244 combines baseline cognitive and clinical scores and APOE4 with FreeSurfer regional morphometry; P-356 uses three hippocampal T1 slices and no clinical data. Not shown to be sufficient: P-244 prints no MRI-only model.
candidate_explanations.quote: we concatenated the baseline clinical features and neuroimaging features extracted from the MRI scans, embedded with t through a transformer encoder, to map to z.

candidate_explanations.difference: Predictor set (P-356 side): image features only.
candidate_explanations.quote: In this work, we solely focused on MRI features, a choice that provides useful information while remaining relatively more accessible compared to other modalities

candidate_explanations.difference: Estimand and label construction: a time-dependent AUC from a survival model over all MCI participants with censoring, against a binary AUC on a cleaned dichotomy that excludes reverters and requires 3 years of stability.
candidate_explanations.quote: of which 348 (44.44%) samples were converted from MCI to AD dementia while the others (55.56%) were right censored.

candidate_explanations.difference: Label construction (P-356 side): reverters excluded, stable MCI required to hold status for at least three years.
candidate_explanations.quote: Individuals in the sMCI group were categorized as stable if they retained this status for a minimum of three years and maintained it throughout all available follow-up assessments provided by ADNI.

candidate_explanations.difference: Model design: P-244's latent pattern is formed from the baseline features together with the patient's progression time, which may make its discrimination estimates optimistic; the held text does not show how test-fold predictions avoid using t.
candidate_explanations.quote: The pattern for an individual patient is formalized as a latent representation z which can be derived given the baseline clinical and neuroimaging characteristics x of the patient as well as the patient’s progression time t.

candidate_explanations.difference: Validation design and inclusion: five-fold CV among participants with at least two MRI scans, against a repeated subject-level 70/15/15 split with about 86 test subjects.
candidate_explanations.quote: Patients from each dataset were eligible for study inclusion if they had at least two T1-weighted volumetric MRI scans.

reason: Both papers predict MCI-to-AD progression in ADNI on a shared MRI channel and report AUC. At the matched horizon, P-244's 3-year AUC of 0.914 and P-356's 36-month AUC of 0.74 each lie outside the other's derived interval (P-356 [0.634, 0.846]; P-244 no lower than 0.858 at any plausible n), and neither study meets the near-ceiling exclusion. Neither paper reports a result under the other's input condition, so the candidate explanations (P-244's clinical scores, its survival estimand with censoring, its use of progression time in forming the latent pattern, and the validation design) are not shown to be sufficient.

quotes.quote: The cohort comprised 575 individuals (299 stable MCIs; 276 progressive MCIs who converted within 36 months) from whom axial T1-weighted MRI slices covering the hippocampal region were used as model inputs.
The data were split into training (70%), validation (15%), and test (15%) sets, while maintaining a constant sMCI/pMCI subject ratio across all splits.
On average, the model achieved an AUC-ROC of 0.74 with a standard deviation of 0.02 and a range of 0.72 to 0.78
AUC (CN→MCI, 3 years 0.802, 5 years 0.876; MCI→AD, 3 years 0.914, 5 years 0.957).
For evaluation, we applied five-fold cross validation
It is worth noting that our model is largely superior to the survival analysis models using MMSE (0.537–0.600) or APOE4 (0.564–0.681) as predictors
Similarly, we achieved an average C-Index of 0.718 (95% CI 0.712–0.725) for predicting the conversion time from MCI to AD dementia.
